subject: Vocabulary
description: High-hit synonym pairs from SSC/banking PYQ; common confusion clusters

questions.explanation: BENEVOLENT (Latin bene = well + volens = wishing) = kind, well-meaning, charitable. Synonyms: kind-hearted, generous, philanthropic, magnanimous, altruistic. Antonym: malevolent (mal = bad + volens = wishing) — wishing harm. Common SSC pair: benevolent vs benefactor (a benevolent person; a benefactor is one who gives money/help).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: AMELIORATE (Latin meliorare = to make better) = to make better; improve. Used for situations, conditions, suffering. 'The new policy will ameliorate the lives of farmers.' Synonyms: improve, enhance, upgrade, rectify, alleviate. Antonym: aggravate, worsen, exacerbate. Common SSC PYQ word.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: CANDID = frank, honest, straightforward; saying what one thinks openly. 'A candid opinion.' Synonyms: frank, honest, forthright, blunt, straightforward, open. Antonyms: evasive, deceitful, secretive. Note: 'candid camera' = catching someone unaware (different sense — natural, unposed).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: OBSTINATE (Latin obstinare = to persist) = stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion. 'Obstinate refusal to listen.' Synonyms: stubborn, headstrong, intransigent, adamant, mulish, pigheaded, recalcitrant. Antonyms: flexible, compliant, accommodating. SSC PYQ pair: obstinate vs obdurate (similar — both stubborn).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: PROCRASTINATE (Latin pro = forward + cras = tomorrow) = to put off; delay action habitually. 'I procrastinated on submitting the form.' Synonyms: postpone, defer, delay, dawdle, dally, stall. Antonyms: expedite, hasten. Procrastination = the noun. PYQ-favourite SSC vocab word.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: METICULOUS (Latin meticulosus = fearful, in turn from metus = fear → fear of error) = showing great attention to detail; very careful + precise. 'Meticulous record-keeping.' Synonyms: thorough, painstaking, careful, scrupulous, diligent, fastidious. Antonyms: careless, sloppy, slipshod.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: FRUGAL = sparing in use of resources; thrifty. 'A frugal meal.' 'Frugal lifestyle.' Synonyms: thrifty, economical, prudent, sparing, parsimonious, austere. Antonyms: extravagant, lavish, wasteful, prodigal. Note: 'frugal' = positive; 'miserly/stingy' = same idea but negative.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Which of the following best captures the meaning of 'LOQUACIOUS'?

options.option_text: prone to speaking at great length
having a quiet and reserved disposition
fond of solitude and deep silence

questions.explanation: A is correct because LOQUACIOUS means excessively talkative or prone to speaking at great length; it shares roots with 'eloquent' (Latin: loqui = to speak). Option B is the antonym — taciturn means quiet and reserved — a classic trap examiners set by pairing loquacious with its opposite.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'PENSIVE'?

options.option_text: acting in a hasty and reckless manner
overly confident in one's own abilities

questions.explanation: C is correct because PENSIVE means deeply absorbed in thought, often with a tinge of sadness or melancholy; synonyms include meditative, contemplative, wistful. Option B (cheerful, light-hearted) is a common wrong choice since candidates link 'pensive' loosely to 'positive' — a false etymology trap.

questions.stem: The word 'EPHEMERAL' is closest in meaning to which of the following?

options.option_text: lasting for only a very brief time

questions.explanation: A is correct because EPHEMERAL (from Greek 'ephemeros' = lasting a day) means short-lived or transient; PYQ usage often appears with 'fame', 'beauty', or 'trends'. Option B (permanent and enduring) is the antonym 'perennial' — examiners frequently offer the antonym as a lure for unprepared candidates.

questions.stem: Which option is the best SYNONYM of 'INSOLVENT'?

options.option_text: skilled in financial and business management
unable to meet outstanding financial obligations
generous in freely distributing personal wealth

questions.explanation: C is correct because INSOLVENT means being unable to pay one's debts when due — equivalent to bankrupt or ruined financially. Option B (cautious about spending) describes frugality, not insolvency; both relate to money, making it a plausible distractor for candidates who confuse money-caution with financial failure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the closest synonym of 'VERBOSE'?

options.option_text: brief and perfectly direct in expression
using far more words than are needed
clear and immediately easy to understand

questions.explanation: B is correct because VERBOSE (Latin: verbosus = full of words) means wordy or using excessive words; synonyms include prolix, long-winded, garrulous. Option C (technical terminology) describes jargon or pedantry — a strong distractor because both make writing difficult to read, but for different reasons.

questions.stem: Choose the synonym that best matches 'RECONDITE' as used in scholarly writing?

options.option_text: dealing with obscure and little-known subject matter
clear and easily grasped by any reader
relating to everyday and practical life skills
widely known and very commonly referenced

questions.explanation: A is correct because RECONDITE means abstruse or dealing with obscure knowledge known only to a few specialists; synonyms include esoteric, arcane, abstruse. Option D (widely known and commonly referenced) is the antonym — examiners love this word because candidates often confuse it with 'recounted' (to narrate), causing them to pick Option C.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines a 'SYCOPHANT'?

options.option_text: one who offers harsh and blunt criticism
a person who gains favour through servile flattery
a principled leader who inspires team courage
an independent thinker of strong moral conviction

questions.explanation: B is correct because SYCOPHANT means a self-seeking flatterer or 'yes-man' who uses insincere praise to gain personal advantage; synonyms include toady, fawner, bootlicker. Option A (harsh blunt criticism) describes a 'critic' or 'cynic' — the exact opposite behavior — making it the most tempting wrong choice for candidates who confuse sycophancy with cynicism.
